\section*{Question 3}

An object moves along the \(x\)-axis with initial position \(x(0)=2\). The velocity of the object at time \(t \geq 0\) is given by \(v(t)=\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{3} t\right)\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] What is the acceleration of the object at time \(t=4\) ?
\item[(b)] Consider the following two statements.
Statement I: For \(3<t<4.5\), the velocity of the object is decreasing.
Statement II: For \(3<t<4.5\), the speed of the object is increasing.
Are either or both of these statements correct? For each statement provide a reason why it is correct or not correct.
\item[(c)] What is the total distance traveled by the object over the time interval \(0 \leq t \leq 4\) ?
\item[(d)] What is the position of the object at time \(t=4\) ?
\item[(a)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(4) & =v^{\prime}(4)=\frac{\pi}{3} \cos \left(\frac{4 \pi}{3}\right) \\
& =-\frac{\pi}{6} \text { or }-0.523 \text { or }-0.524
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] On \(3<t<4.5\) :
\[
a(t)=v^{\prime}(t)=\frac{\pi}{3} \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{3} t\right)<0
\]
Statement I is correct since \(a(t)<0\).
Statement II is correct since \(v(t)<0\) and \(a(t)<0\).
\item[(c)] Distance \(=\int_{0}^{4}|v(t)| d t=2.387\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& x(t)=-\frac{3}{\pi} \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{3} t\right)+\frac{3}{\pi}+2 \\
& x(0)=2 \\
& x(4)=2+\frac{9}{2 \pi}=3.43239 \\
& v(t)=0 \text { when } t=3 \\
& x(3)=\frac{6}{\pi}+2=3.90986 \\
& |x(3)-x(0)|+|x(4)-x(3)|=\frac{15}{2 \pi}=2.387
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(d)] \(x(4)=x(0)+\int_{0}^{4} v(t) d t=3.432\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{OR} \\
& x(t)=-\frac{3}{\pi} \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{3} t\right)+\frac{3}{\pi}+2 \\
& x(4)=2+\frac{9}{2 \pi}=3.432
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
